title: Do Jailbreaks Lobotomize? Measuring Capability Tax of Successful Attacks

original_idea.body:
# Do Jailbreaks Lobotomize? Measuring Capability Tax of Successful Attacks

For a fixed open model, apply several jailbreaks and measure post-jailbreak capability (GSM8K/MMLU subsets) vs StrongREJECT willingness, producing a capability tax per attack type. Inference only, no training (StrongREJECT, arXiv:2402.10260).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 3: plausible chain (better threat-model calibration) but reduced-capability-under-attack doesn't directly map to a concrete catastrophe.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: inherited methodology (apply attacks, run benchmark subsets); refusal-direction ablation adds mild complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 4: focused deliverable (capability tax vs willingness per attack) with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: fuzzy-reward eval on open model, no internal access, weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on one open model plus benchmark subsets, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: StrongREJECT noted the effect but per-attack-type capability-tax measurement appears open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Capability tax observed in prior work but not systematically measured per attack type.
